Apple is about to embark on its major push into the smart home market. A new report published today by Bloomberg reveals that Apple has three brand-new smart home devices that are "nearly ready." The first two products are expected to launch in just two months……

Apple's three new smart home products are about to debut

According to the report, Apple plans to launch a brand-new Apple TV set-top box and an updated HomePod mini as early as this autumn. These products "look similar to current versions," but will feature faster chips to support Siri artificial intelligence capabilities.

For some background, the current Apple TV 4K uses the A15 Bionic chip. Meanwhile, the current HomePod mini is equipped with the S5 chip, which is the same processor found in the Apple Watch Series 5.

Even more exciting is that Apple's highly anticipated new smart home hub device is also "nearly ready." According to the report, this product is tentatively scheduled to make its debut between "October and early next year."

There are currently two versions of this product in development. One "features a display mounted on a semicircular base," while the other is designed to be attached to the wall using a "new magnetic mounting system."

Today's report also once again mentioned the specifications and features of this device. It is reported to feature a 7-inch square display, with Siri AI at its core. The device runs a "brand-new operating system" built on top of tvOS. The interface is described as a "hybrid" of tvOS and watchOS, featuring apps, icons, and widgets.

The device will also support FaceTime, home security monitoring, HomeKit integration, as well as custom watch faces similar to those on the Apple Watch.

However, the most prominent feature is expected to be facial recognition:

Finally, Bloomberg noted that Apple has two other smart home products in development that will launch later. These include a "higher-end, mechanical version of the home hub" with a 9-inch display, as well as an "advanced indoor security camera."
